narrative_shape: A healthy authoring run on the assembler. Orientation reads (36 across 20 paths) and first edits by T75, then an edit/test cycle that keeps correcting concrete defects (bsmr_offset mutation T74, hard-coded field lengths T86-90, MHT/MHR constants T98, test coordinates T118, decode-back T120). Mid-run it reworks has_bmt to be content-driven (T128-132), writes the contract-conformant builder (T148, T159) and gets tests green (T160-161). The tail turns into a wait: Perth-fixture extraction in the background with a monitor (T165-180). No pivot or thrash is visible.

early_signals.signal: Early self-correction ('not frozen, mutate directly') followed by edits; edit count rises 3->7 by T90
narration growing (1.0k->1.65k chars) while verifying exact hex values against a prior session's inspection
alldata_writer.py re-read 12x, but paired with 9 edits (focused iteration, not a loop)
T118-120 loop is fix coordinates -> build -> decode back; context stable, only 4 compactions

rationale: Edit counts and narration rise steadily, re-reads are paired with edits, compaction stays low. No early evidence of thrash or a pivot; the only change of character is the final wait on a long extraction, which is expected work rather than failure.
